subject: Civil Engineering
title: Lateral Force Resisting Systems
description: A micro-lesson that makes Lateral Force Resisting Systems usable.

hook.text: Gravity holds buildings up. But earthquakes push sideways — what resists lateral force?

buildup.text: Moment frames use rigid beam-column connections — they flex but hold together.

discovery.text: Braced frames add diagonal steel members — triangles resist lateral loads efficiently.

twist.text: Shear walls are solid panels — concrete or steel — that act like vertical cantilever beams.

climax.text: Most tall buildings combine systems — shear core with perimeter moment frames.

punchline.text: Earthquakes attack from the side. Every building needs a system to push back.

quiz.question: How do braced frames resist lateral earthquake forces?
options: They use heavy concrete weights at the top to counterbalance swaying
Diagonal steel members form triangles that efficiently resist sideways loads
They disconnect from the foundation to allow free movement
